chapter_theme: A song at Aththippattu (அத்திப்பட்டு): the poet follows a death through the bier, the pyre and the mourners' return home, where Kama soon has them laughing again, and asks for the way to heaven and the golden feet; the praise names Parvati's penance at Kanchi and Vishnu as uncle.

895.reading: The poet pictures death: sense gone, the life leaves, kin cry, drums beat, the body is set on a golden bier, laid on the pyre with rice from flower hands and cloth, the Vedas recited, and burned in crackling fire; the mourners bathe, go home and forget their grief, and wicked Kama with his flowers makes them laugh and weep again. Thinking of his servant, worn out in women's hands, the poet asks Murugan to tell him 'this is the way to heaven' and give the golden feet. The praise names Murugan the son of the mountain-king's daughter, the green peacock who did her hard penance at Kanchi, the nephew of Vishnu who shot Ravana's ten heads and twenty arms, the one on the emerald peacock who dried the sea and resettled the gods, at Aththippattu of fields where kayal fish leap.
895.nuance: The funeral is told rite by rite (அரிசி இட்டு, கலை, மறைகள், புனல் முழுகி மனை புக்கு), and the turn is that the mourners' grief ends at the bath and Kama takes them again. கச்சியினில் அரிய தவம்: Parvati's penance at Kanchi. The line on the mourners (உறவுநிலை சுட்டுச் சுட்டி) is hard to divide.

links.note: The Naladiyar's man sees kin wailing over a corpse carried to the burning ground and still marries believing there is joy here; 895 follows the mourners home from the pyre, where Kama soon sets them laughing again. Both find the same forgetting at the edge of the burning ground.

895 follows the funeral rite by rite and then the mourners, who bathe in water, go home and lose their grief (மருவுபுனல் முழுகி மனை புக்குத் துக்கமறு). Tirumanthiram 145 ends the same way: they burn him, bathe in water and stop thinking of him (நீரினில் மூழ்கி நினைப்பொழிந்தார்களே). Both make the bath the point where memory of the dead ends; 895 goes on to show desire taking the mourners again.
